 Heat’s defense may have found its missing spark in two unexpected players 
 Myron Gardner and Ryan Conwell has sparked the team. By Michael Saenz | Nov 17, 2026, 10:40 AM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Miami Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra reacts (Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Conwell and Myron Gardner may have given the Miami Heat the exact defensive spark that they've needed. Before the season, I can't imagine there were many who expected it from these two unexpected contributors. 
--> Ryan Conwell and Myron Gardner may have given the Miami Heat the exact defensive spark that they've needed. Before the season, I can't imagine there were many who expected it from these two unexpected contributors. 
 But it's certainly been a welcome surprise for the Heat. 
--> But it's certainly been a welcome surprise for the Heat. 
 Over the last five games, it feels as if there's been a shift within the Heat's defensive dynamic. Through the first few weeks of the season, the Heat had one of the worst defensive ratings in the league. And the eye test matched their poor metrics. 
--> Over the last five games, it feels as if there's been a shift within the Heat's defensive dynamic. Through the first few weeks of the season, the Heat had one of the worst defensive ratings in the league. And the eye test matched their poor metrics. 
 There's been a defensive shift for the Heat 
--> There's been a defensive shift for the Heat 
 However, over the past week and a half, it does feel as if there's been a tangible improvement for the Heat. Interestingly enough, it may have been sparked by Gardner and Conwell, who have gotten a bigger role in the rotation since the improvements. 
--> However, over the past week and a half, it does feel as if there's been a tangible improvement for the Heat. Interestingly enough, it may have been sparked by Gardner and Conwell, who have gotten a bigger role in the rotation since the improvements. 
 After a November 5th loss to the Golden State Warriors, the Heat were 3-6. They had the fifth-worst defensive rating and the seventh-worst net rating. They were a team that appeared without an identity and in a situation that had a real chance of completely spiraling out of control. 
--> After a November 5th loss to the Golden State Warriors, the Heat were 3-6. They had the fifth-worst defensive rating and the seventh-worst net rating. They were a team that appeared without an identity and in a situation that had a real chance of completely spiraling out of control. 
 Since then, though, the Heat have won five games in a row. A big part of that winning streak? Besides the dominance of Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo, it's the team's improved defense. Over that span, the Heat have the league's 10th-best defensive rating and the fourth-best net rating. 
--> Since then, though, the Heat have won five games in a row. A big part of that winning streak? Besides the dominance of Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo, it's the team's improved defense. Over that span, the Heat have the league's 10th-best defensive rating and the fourth-best net rating. 
 The spark from Gardner and Conwell has been at the center of it all. And while their production has been hit or miss on most nights, it's their infectious energy and effort that have made all the difference for Miami, especially on the defensive end of the floor. 
--> The spark from Gardner and Conwell has been at the center of it all. And while their production has been hit or miss on most nights, it's their infectious energy and effort that have made all the difference for Miami, especially on the defensive end of the floor. 
 In many ways, Gardner and Conwell bring a level of energy and activity on the defensive side of the court that was missing, the likes of which neither Tim Hardaway Jr. nor Andrew Wiggins were bringing. 
--> In many ways, Gardner and Conwell bring a level of energy and activity on the defensive side of the court that was missing, the likes of which neither Tim Hardaway Jr. nor Andrew Wiggins were bringing. 
 It's clearly made a difference for Miami. Whether most are willing to admit it or not, it does feel as if things began to shift the moment both Conwell and Gardner were getting more opportunities . It could've been a culmination of it all, but there's no question Conwell and Gardner have certainly helped. 
--> It's clearly made a difference for Miami. Whether most are willing to admit it or not, it does feel as if things began to shift the moment both Conwell and Gardner were getting more opportunities . It could've been a culmination of it all, but there's no question Conwell and Gardner have certainly helped. 
 It's at the point that even when the Heat are fully healthy, once Pelle Larsson is back from the illness he's battling, there's a very real chance that Erik Spoelstra sticks with Gardner in the starting lineup . With how the Heat have been playing of late, I'm not sure Spoelstra can risk messing with it now.
--> It's at the point that even when the Heat are fully healthy, once Pelle Larsson is back from the illness he's battling, there's a very real chance that Erik Spoelstra sticks with Gardner in the starting lineup . With how the Heat have been playing of late, I'm not sure Spoelstra can risk messing with it now.
 Could there be a point where Larsson (or even Wiggins) earns the starting nod back? Absolutely. However, especially with how the Heat are playing of late, it would be foolish for Spoelstra to mess with such a good thing.
